name: Video Saturation
description: Profiles chroma saturation histograms and tracks their inter-frame stability to identify the unnaturally uniform or oscillating color intensity patterns produced by video generation models.
mechanism:
This method analyzes video saturation for forensic detection:

1. **Saturation Measurement**: Color saturation is measured per frame in HSV and Lab color spaces. Per-region saturation statistics (mean, variance, distribution shape) capture the color vibrancy characteristics.

2. **Face-Background Saturation Comparison**: Saturation levels of the face and background should be consistent (same camera, same color grading). The method compares saturation statistics — deepfake faces may show different saturation characteristics from the generation model's output color space mapping.

3. **Skin Tone Saturation**: Human skin follows specific saturation ranges dependent on skin type (Fitzpatrick scale). The method checks whether face skin saturation falls within plausible physiological ranges. AI generators may produce oversaturated or undersaturated skin inconsistent with natural skin tones.

4. **Temporal Saturation Stability**: Saturation should vary smoothly over time, consistent with illumination changes. The method tracks saturation stability — high-frequency saturation fluctuations in the face (while background remains stable) indicate per-frame rendering inconsistency from deepfake generation.

5. **Saturation-Luminance Relationship**: In natural images, saturation and luminance show specific relationships (Hunt effect — saturation appears higher at higher luminance). The method checks whether the saturation-luminance relationship follows natural perception models. AI generators may produce content with incorrect saturation-luminance coupling.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through video saturation analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
